It is zero on every other token (including the first token, so there is no floor), zero when the preposition follows a non-motion verb (talked to, listened to, sat on, belongs to, arrived at, welcome to, according to, close to) or a non-directional preposition (from, with, over), and weak (<0.45 of max) for manner-of-motion verbs like walked/drove.

At the elementary school, volunteers stacked cots and filled coolers with bottled water. The Red Cross said the gymnasium could hold three hundred people, though only a fraction of that number had arrived by dusk. Officials warned that the single highway could close without notice, and that anyone who waited too long might find a fallen pine blocking the way. Crews set up generators and strung lights across the fairgrounds while a veterinarian from the county clinic offered to board dogs and cats. Radio stations read the evacuation list every hour, and a line of cars idled along the shoulder, headlights on, waiting for word that the pass was open. Meanwhile, the first convoy of evacuees got to the shelter just after midnight, many of them still in pajamas, some carrying nothing but a phone charger and a pillow. Volunteers handed out blankets and hot soup while a nurse checked blood pressure. A teacher organized a table of board games for the children, and a retired mechanic walked the hallways with a flashlight, checking that every door was latched. Outside, the wind had shifted again, pushing smoke across the parking lot and turning the streetlights orange. Nobody slept much. By three in the morning the gymnasium floor was covered with sleeping bags, and the kitchen crew was already brewing a second pot of coffee. By Thursday the fire had burned more than eighteen thousand acres and was only a third contained. Forecasters saw no rain in the ten-day outlook, and the sheriff said deputies would keep patrolling the empty neighborhoods until the last resident was accounted for. A relief fund at the credit union had collected enough for fuel and groceries, though organizers admitted that rebuilding would take years. For the families now living on cots, the immediate worry was smaller and more urgent: school enrollment, missing paperwork, and whether an insurance adjuster would ever return their calls. A spokesman for the county said temporary housing would be available for at least six weeks, and that caseworkers would visit each family to help with applications. He asked anyone who had left medication behind to call the hotline before attempting to return, since the roads remained closed and the smoke had not cleared.
